question.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $55u+24v=\text{gcd}(55,24).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}55 & = & 24\cdot 2 & + & 7 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 24 & = & 7\cdot 3 & + & 3 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 7 & = & 3\cdot 2 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(55,24)=1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}7 & =55-24\cdot 2 \\ 3 & =24-7\cdot 3 \\ 1 & =7-3\cdot 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =7-3\cdot 2 \\  & =7-[24-7\cdot 3]\cdot 2 \\  & =7\cdot 7-24\cdot 2 \\  & =[55-24\cdot 2]\cdot 7-24\cdot 2 \\  & =55\cdot 7-24\cdot 16 \\  & =55\cdot 7+24\cdot (-16)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=7$ and $v=-16.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=7+(-16)=-9.
$$
